summary: Ohio State takes its offensive-line questions and McCuin’s emergence to Texas. Watch whether the pass rush can finish against Arch Manning. Kickoff is Saturday at 7:30 p.m. ET on ABC.

items.headline: Day keeps the offensive-line lineup under review
items.tldr: Day says Ohio State will keep evaluating its starting group after the opener. Watch who takes the first snaps in Austin and whether the blocking holds up against a stronger test.

items.headline: McCuin gives Sayin another receiver to lean on
items.tldr: His six catches produced 97 yards and a touchdown, with every catch moving the chains or scoring. If Texas shades coverage toward Jeremiah Smith, McCuin’s ability to win elsewhere becomes a key watch point.

items.headline: The pass rush needs to finish against a mobile quarterback
items.tldr: The Dispatch found that Ohio State struggled to bring down Ball State’s quarterback when pressured. Against Arch Manning, watch the pass rush lanes as closely as the pressure: an escape can erase a good start to the play.

items.headline: Sayin opens with 320 passing yards; Texas is next
items.tldr: Ohio State won 56-3, with Jeremiah Smith and Devin McCuin leading the receiving production. The passing game now takes that start on the road to Austin; watch whether the protection lets Sayin keep finding his receivers.

items.headline: Traveling to Austin? DKR’s new map locates gates and water
items.tldr: The interactive map marks seats, concessions, restrooms and first aid on the web and in the Texas Longhorns app. Open it before arriving; step-by-step navigation is still listed as coming soon.

lead.headline: Protect Sayin. Finish the pass rush.
lead.body: Watch the starting offensive line and whether the pass rush can finish against Texas.

matchup.question: What should Ohio State clean up before Texas?
matchup.answer: Day is evaluating the offensive line. On defense, watch whether the pass rush can finish without opening escape lanes.
